title: The Distant Wardrobe
premise: Cyrus Villalobos, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost his sense of taste after his mother's death, is clearing out her condemned house when he finds a cache of undelivered letters hidden behind the wardrobe — letters she wrote to him over thirty years and never sent, each one confessing the truths she couldn't say aloud: his father's abandonment, her illness, her fear that Cyrus had inherited her talent for silence. As the demolition date approaches, Cyrus reads one letter per day, tasting food again for the first time in years as each secret lands. In the end he stands in the empty house on demolition morning, reads the final letter aloud to the bare walls, and finally says goodbye — not by keeping the house, but by keeping the words.
about_author: Wendell Nystrom is the pen name of a former obituary writer who spent a decade composing other people's goodbyes before turning to fiction about the ones we fail to deliver. He lives near a house scheduled for demolition and visits it often.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. We meet him at a tasting menu he cannot taste, writing luminous reviews from memory while his life runs on autopilot. A notice arrives: his late mother's house will be demolished in six weeks unless cleared. Emotional beat: numbness mistaken for peace, cracked by the word 'demolition.'

chapters.title: Behind the Cedar
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Clearing the bedroom, he pulls the wardrobe from the wall and finds a shoebox of sealed, stamped, never-mailed letters addressed to him, dated across three decades. He pockets the first without opening it. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past has been waiting, patient and organized.

chapters.title: Letter One: 1989
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Cyrus reading, and his young mother Marisol writing. The first letter describes the day his father left, written with a warmth Cyrus never witnessed. That night, eating alone, he tastes salt. Emotional beat: grief arriving disguised as flavor.

chapters.title: The Reviewer Who Lied
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. His editor suspects his recent reviews are hollow; a rival critic hints publicly that Villalobos has 'lost his palate.' Cyrus deflects, but the accusation lodges. He skips letter two out of spite. Emotional beat: shame — the professional mask slipping in public.

chapters.title: Letters Three Through Nine
chapters.summary: Marisol's voice dominates as Cyrus binges the box: her cancer diagnosis, her pride in him, her confession that she stopped speaking of love because her own mother never did. He learns silence was an inheritance too. Emotional beat: recognition — he is reading his own future in her handwriting.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Knew
chapters.summary: Cyrus's estranged aunt Rosa's POV. She arrives uninvited to help clear the house, reveals Marisol told her about the letters years ago and made her promise not to interfere. Rosa forces Cyrus to admit he's been living in the house like a guest. Emotional beat: confrontation as reluctant grace.

chapters.title: The Last Letter Is Missing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The box holds every year except the final one — no letter from her last month alive. Convinced it exists, he tears through the house as the demolition crew posts final notices. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into obsession; the house becomes a body being searched.

chapters.title: What the Wardrobe Kept
chapters.summary: Rosa and Cyrus move the wardrobe together and find the last letter taped inside its frame — unfinished, mid-sentence, ending simply: 'Come home while I can still hear you.' Cyrus breaks down; Rosa holds him in the kitchen where they never spoke. Emotional beat: devastation as release.

chapters.title: Demolition Eve
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He publishes a raw personal essay instead of a review — 'On Forgetting How to Taste' — confessing everything, then cooks his mother's caldo in the empty house using her handwritten recipe card. He can taste all of it. Emotional beat: return; the tenant becomes the owner.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Cyrus's POV. On demolition morning he stands in the gutted house and reads the unfinished last letter aloud, finishing the sentence himself, then says goodbye properly — out loud, to the walls, to her. He walks out carrying only the letters. Emotional beat: belonging redefined; inheritance accepted.
